Do you want to help create experiences that surprise and inspire, and fill ÅBEN’s bars with life?

Events give guests a new way to meet ÅBEN. Whether it’s a spontaneous quiz night or a planned company celebration, it’s about inviting guests into the universe and giving them an experience they’ll remember.

We are looking for a sales-driven and hands-on Event Manager who will take responsibility for developing the events area into a stronger part of the bars, from proactive sales and idea development to planning and execution. Success is about bringing more guests into the bars and strengthening revenue through events and private bookings.

Your responsibilities

You will be part of Operations and report to the Bar Operations Manager. You will be working closely with the individual Bar Managers and the Event Coordinator for Kødbyen on a daily basis. The position is anchored in the bars and on the events that are part of everyday life at ÅBEN, both commercial bookings and the public, recurring formats. Brand and partnership events are run by Marketing, but you will work closely with the team to develop and sharpen them. You will also stay in close dialogue with Marketing, so that all formats live up to ÅBEN’s values: creating joy through experiences, daring to walk our own path, making an effort, and doing the right thing, even when no one is watching.

Event Manager is a new role, which gives you the opportunity to shape it from the very beginning. This means a responsibility to create structure and direction, and the freedom to test new ideas and shape how events work across the bars. Your responsibilities cover a wide range:

• 
Proactive sales and day-to-day dialogue with both private guests and companies.

• 
Project management from first enquiry to final follow-up, including pricing, budgets, planning and review.

• 
Development of new concepts and recurring formats that fit the bars and turn first-time guests into regulars.

• 
Optimising sales channels, booking sites and internal processes to make the most of the bars’ capacity.

• 
Synergy and shared standards across the bars, with room to find what works for each individual bar.

• 
Presence at larger events to ensure quality and support the bar staff.

Who are you?

We expect you to thrive in a fast-paced environment with an informal tone and a flat structure. You have a strong eye for the big picture, naturally take the lead and can balance structure at the desk with presence on the floor. We imagine that you:

• 
Have at least 3 years of experience with sales, planning and running events, preferably from the restaurant, hotel or entertainment industry.

• 
Have a good commercial understanding and find it motivating to work with sales targets, budgets and getting the most out of every bar.

• 
Are a strong communicator and relationship builder who works effortlessly with both guests and bar staff.

• 
Understand or are interested in ÅBEN’s brand and can turn the values into concrete guest experiences.

• 
Thrive in a flexible day-to-day and are comfortable lending a hand in operations when things get busy.

Ready for the next step?

Becoming part of ÅBEN means stepping into an organisation in development with both ambitions and its heart in the right place. There is room to grow, take responsibility and have fun along the way.

The position is full-time, and you will be based at the office in Kødbyen, with presence at the other bars when needed. Events typically take place in the evenings and at weekends, so some flexibility comes with the job.

Interviews are held continuously, so send your application today if the role of Event Manager at ÅBEN sounds like something for you.

As our next Technical Project Manager in the Data & Migrations team, you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups — locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most

About the role

This is a Senior role designed to provide program leadership to deliver strategic technical solutions that address complex client issues in the Life Sciences industry. As a manager within the Migration team, you will be handling projects and programs with regards to migration implementation to achieve desired outcomes and ensure successful business growth and regulatory compliance. You will also seek new business opportunities to help BASE life science grow its presence within existing and new customers.

You will provide program/project management oversight for all customer implementations falling under the Migrations team’s scope.

You will lead project teams consisting of data engineers/scientists. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in data engineering, project management and the ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications.

As a Technical Project Manager for the Migration team your responsibilities include:

• Monitoring program status including milestones, risks, issues, budgets, etc.

• Acting as a delivery escalation point and proactively ensuring escalations are handled promptly with a clear action and communication plan.

• Providing executive level summaries for senior executives in BASE life science.

• Intervening, when necessary, to ensure costs, timelines and quality are on track.

• Developed plans and effort estimates for future project during sales process.

Delivering Projects:

• Lead a cross-functional team to deliver data driven projects on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our life science industry stakeholders.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders in the life science industry to understand their data needs and translate them into technical specifications for the project team.

• Develop project plans, timelines, and budgets for the projects.

• Track and report on project progress, identifying and mitigating risks as needed.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration between the project team, life science industry stakeholders, and other teams within BASE life science.

What makes you the best person for this job?

• 5+ years of experience as a technical project manager ideally within the life science industry or other regulated areas.

• Successful track record of managing technically complex projects such as software development, implementation of IT systems, data migrations, etc.

• Experience leading developers, data engineers and/or data scientists and delivering data driven projects.

• Experience with project management tools such as JIRA.

• Experience with Agile project management methodologies such as SAFe.

• Strong communication skills, both in writing, meetings and in presentations.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.

• A genuine interest in understanding the technical aspects of complex data-driven projects.

Additionally, the ideal candidate has the following qualifications:

• Experience with coding in Python, VBA, Java, R, SQL, C, or similar.

• Experience selling either projects or products to clients.

• Experience working with Veeva Vault.

This position is offered in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2007, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting enterprise working exclusively in the life sciences industry.

With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Europe and the United States, we support clients globally. We work closely with our customers to identify, develop, and implement initiatives that drive growth, efficiency, and meaningful change. Through partnerships with leading solution providers such as Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Benchling, and MediSpend, we help our clients unlock the full potential of modern technologies.

Why join BASE Life Science?

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact.

You will be part of a collaborative, high‑performing environment where:

• Ambition is encouraged through ownership and continuous learning

• Execution matters — we focus on delivering solutions that work in practice

• Team spirit and trust guide collaboration across roles, countries, and disciplines

• Openness means your ideas are heard, you are challenged constructively, and supported as you grow

Alongside this, we offer:

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance

• A modern work setup, with the tools and equipment needed to do great work

• Recognition of performance and impact, linked to contribution and results

Do you have experience in managing complex operations contracts and commercial risk across countries? Do you enjoy building something into the next level?

We are looking for a Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to take end-to-end ownership of operations contracts across Eurowind Energy's global wind, solar and BESS portfolio.

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to join our Global Operations team. Based at our Operations office in Hobro, you will be the contract and warranty specialist for our global asset portfolio, supporting colleagues and managers across countries and functions.

Your role

As Senior Contract and Warranty Manager, you will take ownership of key commercial agreements, claims and warranty matters across Eurowind Energy's global asset portfolio. You will work closely with Asset Management, Operations, Finance, Legal and local teams to ensure that our contractual rights are understood, protected and actively used. The role combines hands-on contract management with a strong focus on risk, value creation and standardization across markets.

• Own contract management for operations contracts, including service and O&M agreements, warranty and performance guarantees, grid connection and curtailment compensation, insurance, land lease and supplier agreements

• Lead negotiation, drafting and execution of contracts so they meet both legal and commercial requirements

• Identify, assess and mitigate commercial and legal risk across the contract portfolio

• Manage claims and warranty follow-up, making sure issues are tracked, escalated and resolved in line with contractual terms

• Build global contract templates, playbooks and governance processes that work consistently across countries

• Monitor contract performance and compliance, flagging risks and improvement opportunities

• Be the go-to contact for the country teams and the wider operations organisation on contract questions and disputes

You will work with the country operations teams, Strategic Commercial Management (which owns PPAs, power trading and balancing contracts), Technical Operations, Investor Administration, SCADA Operations, Legal, Finance, and suppliers and service providers. Your role is to strengthen the countries' ability to manage contracts locally, not to add another layer of bureaucracy.

What we offer

You will join Global Operations at a time where we are transforming how we manage and operate our global asset portfolio. You will get a broad international scope, close collaboration across functions and countries, and the opportunity to work with complex commercial and operational challenges. We offer a high level of autonomy, a strong professional environment and the opportunity to make a visible impact on how Eurowind operates.

• A newly created role where you set the structures and ways of working

• The chance to make a real impact on how we improve and operate our commercial mindset

• Ownership, trust and room to shape your own area

• A global role with some travel, in an international and energetic environment

• A workplace in Hobro, alongside our operations colleagues

You will join a newly established team and report to Louise Guldager Thomsen, Head of Global Commercial Management. Louise is a collaborative and pragmatic leader who builds strong relationships, creates alignment across functions and empowers people to take ownership. She combines a deep understanding of the organisation with a practical focus on execution and a global perspective.

Required competencies and skills

You have solid experience with contract management, commercial agreements, warranties and/or claims, ideally from the energy, infrastructure, construction or other asset-intensive industries. You are comfortable navigating complex contractual matters and working across technical, commercial and legal topics. You combine strong analytical and negotiation skills with a pragmatic approach and the ability to turn contractual knowledge into action and business value.

• Significant experience in contract management within energy, infrastructure, renewables or another asset-intensive industry

• A proven record of leading complex contract negotiations end-to-end, including service and O&M, warranty, grid/curtailment, insurance and supplier contracts

• Solid understanding of commercial and legal risk management, with experience building or applying compliance frameworks

• Relevant legal, commercial or technical education (for example law, business or engineering), or equivalent hands-on experience

• International experience and comfort working across countries and cultures

• Enjoys building something new and setting up structures from scratch

• Works autonomously across a global organisation and values being part of a team

• Structured and detail-oriented, yet pragmatic about getting things done without unnecessary process

• Communicates clearly and directly, holding suppliers and internal stakeholders accountable while working with respect

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record.

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. Do you want to make sure that when something goes wrong, our organisation already knows what to do? Are you energised by building capability and confidence in others, rather than being the one who has to solve every incident yourself?

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Global Resilience Consultant to join our team in Hobro, Denmark.

As an operator of critical energy infrastructure, our ability to respond when things go wrong is fundamental to protecting our business, our partners and the communities we serve. As Eurowind continues to grow and face an evolving risk landscape and regulatory requirements such as NIS2, we are strengthening emergency preparedness as an integrated part of the organisation – in every market where we operate.

You will join our Group Cyber and Information Security team – a small, senior team supporting a global organisation, anchored directly with the CISO. Emergency preparedness is coordinated centrally from Group headquarters across all our markets, and we do not scale through headcount alone, but through clear plans, practised people and smart use of technology. That means real ownership, meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to shape how prepared Eurowind is when it matters most.

Your role

This is a new and highly visible role. As Group Emergency Preparedness Advisor, you own that Eurowind is ready before a crisis happens – not that you personally run the response when one occurs. You make sure our global emergency preparedness has the plans it needs, that those plans are kept current and fit for purpose across all markets, and that the people who will use them are trained and confident enough to act.

You will not run our incident response or crisis management yourself, and you are not expected to. That responsibility stays with the teams and leaders whose job it is to respond when something happens. Your job is to build and maintain the framework behind them – the plans, the training and the exercises – so that when a crisis hits, everyone already knows their role.

Your work will include:

• Owning Eurowind’s global emergency preparedness framework – making sure the crisis management, business continuity and incident response plans we need actually exist, across all markets

• Mapping which plans are in place, where, and identifying and closing gaps together with local management and Group functionsin

• Driving larger, cross-market crisis exercises as well as frequent smaller micro-exercises – so readiness is tested and kept sharp continuously, not just checked off once a year

• Making sure plans and training cover the full range of scenarios relevant to Eurowind – from cyber incidents to safety events, operational disruptions and OT/critical infrastructure incidents

• Working with country management, Group functions such as security, legal, communications and HR, and site teams to keep plans realistic and grounded in how the organisation actually operates

• Reporting on preparedness status, training coverage and identified gaps back to the CISO and contributing to Group-level prioritisation

What we offer

We believe preparedness only counts if it works under pressure. A plan nobody has practised is not a plan – it is a document. That is exactly what this role is about: making sure Eurowind is drilled, not just documented.

We are moving towards an approach that is more structured, tested and better integrated across the business. Our role is not to own every response, but to make sure Eurowind can respond – confidently and consistently – globally, under NIS2 and in an increasingly demanding risk landscape.

We also believe good preparedness starts with strong fundamentals. It is easy to write an impressive plan, but most organisations are exposed because the basics are not consistently trained and practised. For us, that means clear ownership, tested plans and people who know what to do – consistently, in every market. We do not dismiss ambition – we build the foundation that makes it viable.

Just as importantly, we believe better preparedness comes from building a better team. We value people who challenge assumptions, think independently and bring different perspectives. Leadership in our team is about creating the conditions for better answers to emerge, not pretending to have all the answers.

In return, you will get:

• A unique, self-directed role with international reach and direct impact across 14 countries

• Direct anchoring with the CISO and close collaboration with senior stakeholders across the Group

• A clear mandate to build capability rather than carry the operational burden alone – you own the framework, not every incident

• Access to modern AI tools and automation to amplify your impact

• Pension and health insurance

• Flexible working hours and a hybrid working model based at our headquarters in Hobro – with the opportunity to travel to our European markets when it makes a difference

Required competencies and skills

This role is less about being the person in the room during a crisis, and more about the discipline and drive to make sure everyone else knows what to do when they are. You are comfortable walking into a country office or an energy park and earning trust quickly – whether you are talking to a country manager, a site technician or a Group specialist. You know how to turn “we should probably have a plan for that” into a plan people have actually practised.

We imagine you bring:

• Solid experience within crisis management, business continuity or emergency preparedness, for example from consulting, advisory or a broad security or resilience role in an international organisation

• A structured and analytical way of working – you can map the current state, spot the gaps and turn them into concrete plans and training

• Experience designing and delivering exercises at different scales – from full crisis simulations to quick, recurring micro-exercises

• Strong stakeholder management skills and the credibility to engage with local management across cultures

• A working understanding of regulatory frameworks relevant to preparedness, such as NIS2

• Excellent communication skills in English; additional European languages are an advantage

• Willingness to travel occasionally across our 14 markets

It’s a plus if you have:

• Experience from the energy sector or other critical infrastructure

• Experience working in a Group/HQ function delivering services to local entities

• Familiarity with standards such as ISO 22301 (business continuity) or IEC 62443 (OT security)

• Used AI or LLMs as practical tools in your workflow

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record. A security clearance may become relevant later in the employment, but it is not required in order to apply.

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy A/S on our website or LinkedIn

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Global Drug Safety & Pharmacovigilance Physician
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**This role provides medical oversight of product safety, including adverse event review, ongoing safety surveillance, and management of emerging safety issues. Responsibilities include safety input to clinical and regulatory deliverables, aggregate reporting, safety committee oversight, cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.

**Responsibilities

**

• Perform medical review of Adverse Events reports for Genmab products.

• Perform ongoing surveillance of safety data from Genmab clinical trials.

• Ensure handling of safety issues.

• Perform medical review and provide input to e.g., Trial Protocols and amendments, Trial Reports, Trial plans, eCRFs/CRFs, TMFs, Investigator’s Brochures, Subject Informed Consent, Development Safety Update Reports, Integrated Safety Summaries, scientific articles, and medical reviews.

• Prepare aggregated reports and safety summaries in accordance with regulatory requirements.

• Responsible for the establishment and management of external Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs)

• Chair and manage Genmab Safety Committees

• Conduct training of Genmab employees, CROs and Investigators

• Member of Clinical Management Teams (CMTs), Compound Development Teams (CDT) and Compound Strategy Teams (CST) and contribute to multidisciplinary project groups and provide input to clinical development programs.

• Interact with safety and clinical CROs and perform sponsor oversight activities.

• Collaborate with external experts and partners.

• Contribute to multidisciplinary project groups.

• Ensure compliance with regulatory guidelines and internal procedures in order to be prepared for audits and inspections.

• Participate in audit and inspection activities as relevant

**Requirements

**

• Medical degree (MD or equivalent) with relevant clinical experience; oncology or hematology experience preferred.

• 8+ years of experience in pharmacovigilance, drug safety, or clinical development within the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry.

• Demonstrated experience in adverse event medical review, safety surveillance, signal evaluation, benefit–risk assessment, and aggregate safety reporting.

• Experience providing medical safety input to clinical trials and regulatory deliverables, including protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, informed consent documents, DSURs, clinical study reports, and integrated safety summaries.

• Strong knowledge of global pharmacovigilance and clinical development requirements, with experience supporting Safety Committees/DMCs, regulatory submissions, audits, and inspections.

• Strong medical judgment, leadership, and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate across functions, CROs, external partners, and regulatory stakeholders.

• Experience executing processes/projects in own area (e.g. guidance documents as per intl. regulations & reporting requirements; preparation of post-marketing spontaneous and clinical trial safety assessments; regulatory submissions; safety case processing; PV data systems; safety data base systems and the report generation)

• Experience working with FDA/EMA/PMDA/ICH requirements, good clinical practices, and pharmaceutical clinical development

• Experience guiding team members around complex issues

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$200,000.00---$300,000.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

jobs.occupation: Scientific programmer and data analyst in Environmental Science
jobs.description:
Would you like to apply your programming and data analysis skills to research and environmental advisory work addressing air pollution and climate change? We are looking for a scientific programmer and data analyst to help develop, modernize and operate atmospheric models and analyze complex environmental datasets. You will join the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling at the Department of Environmental Science, Aarhus University, working closely with researchers on both scientific projects and research-based advice to public authorities. 

The Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling conducts research and provides research-based advice on atmospheric processes, emission inventories, air pollution and climate modeling, integrated impact assessment for health, nature and climate, and land-use and remote-sensing research. You will play an important role in advancing this work through the development and improvement of scientific models and the analysis and interpretation of complex environmental data.

This is a permanent position based in Roskilde, Denmark, with an expected starting date of February 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a permanent position starting 1 Feb 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
You will participate in research and advisory projects, the latter mainly for the Danish Ministry of Environment. Both research and advisory projects aim to understand atmospheric processes, helping ministries and environmental agencies regulate air quality and protect our environment. You will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary team of researchers. 

Together with researchers, your main task will be to restructure, improve and modernize existing air quality models and forecast systems as well as to contribute to the development of new integrated air pollution models. A key part of your role will be to help modernize our scientific codebase by introducing and applying good software development practices, making our models and workflows easier to maintain, document, test and reproduce. Your tasks will also include developing and automating workflows for computationally demanding model simulations, including parallel computing, and the processing of large datasets, as well as developing and maintaining applications and scripts in Linux and Windows environments.

You will have the opportunity to collaborate with various research groups and shape the Section’s data science strategy. In addition, you will take part in department-wide initiatives such as workshops, presentations and events related to data science, and contribute to reports and scientific publications.

Your profile
We welcome applications from candidates who meet most, though not necessarily all, of the following qualifications:

 * An MSc or PhD in computer science, software engineering, physics, applied mathematics or a related field
 * Advanced programming skills in languages such as Python, R, Fortran, C/C++ or similar, including experience with scientific computing, data analysis and visualization libraries
 * Experience with implementing and applying modern software development practices for scientific computing, including code organization, version control, documentation, testing, maintainability and reproducibility, as well as experience with parallel computing
 * Experience in handling and analyzing large datasets

We are looking for a curious, proactive and motivated colleague who is keen to develop new technical skills and acquire knowledge of atmospheric and air pollution science. Experience with the development and application of air quality models would be welcome, but is not required.

You should enjoy working both independently and collaboratively, sharing knowledge and providing technical guidance to colleagues. Good communication skills and excellent written and spoken English are important. Danish language skills are an advantage, but not a requirement.

Additional experience in any of the following areas would be an advantage, but is not required:
 * GIS and geospatial data
 * Development and integration of APIs and web-based applications
 * Working with and modernizing legacy scientific software, including Delphi or similar technologies
 * Machine learning and AI methods

About the Department 
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department within the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. Our research covers a wide range of fields, including physics, chemistry, microbiology, social sciences, geography, and environmental economics. The department conducts research and provides research-based advice to ministries and public authorities. Our work addresses major societal challenges such as pollution control, land and water management, climate change, biodiversity protection, and ecosystem services.

We have a highly collaborative work environment, where all employees contribute to securing the research and advisory projects that fund the majority of the department’s activities. We value equality, diversity, and a strong work-life balance.

The Research Group

The selected candidate will join the Atmospheric Modelling Group within the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling. The group focuses on air pollution processes and climate interactions. It develops, tests, and applies models across spatial scales, from global to local, and examines the environmental, health, and socioeconomic impacts of air pollution and climate change. Close collaboration with other sections within the department is essential, particularly in areas such as atmospheric measurements, environmental economics, and geography.

In the group, we specialize in 
 * Atmospheric physics and chemistry, including numerical methods and computer science
 * Air pollution modeling at global, regional (Northern Hemisphere, Europe, Denmark) and local scales (urban areas, point sources)
 * Numerical weather prediction models at different spatial scales
 * Integrated assessment modeling (impact on health, environment, and climate)
 * Environmental noise modeling
 * Climate modeling and its links to air pollution and health
 * Decision-support for policy makers on emissions, air quality, and health impacts

Work location 

The place of work will be at Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located approx. 30 km from Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits. 

International candidates may find information concerning living and working in Denmark at www.workindenmark.dk. AU International Center offers a full range of services to make your transition to Denmark as smooth as possible (http://www.au.dk/en/internationalcentre/ias/), and the department will assist foreign candidates with finding a suitable place to live.

Contact information

Further information may be obtained from Professor Peter Langen, Head of the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling, at plangen@envs.au.dk or +45 2061 8369.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 3 Dec 2026.

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between either the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions, where you will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8, or subject to section 15 of the collective agreement for IT employees (PROSA) in the service of the state and LC/CO10-S (the Confederation of Teachers’ Unions/the Danish Confederation of Public Employees of 2010) collective agreement.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Department of Public Health at the Faculty of Health Sciences – Aarhus University invites applications for a position as Professor and Director of The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTbiomed). The starting date is 1st June 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a permanent full-time position. The director of SMARTbiomed is based at Aarhus University, Denmark.

About SMARTbiomed
The Pioneer Centre for SMARTbiomed is funded by a combined grant of DKK 250 million from the Lundbeck Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, the Villum Foundation, the Carlsberg Foundation and the Danish National Research Foundation. The Centre is funded for 13 years, starting in June 2024, and currently consists of approximately 60 researchers at all levels and support staff. SMARTbiomed is anchored at the National Centre for Register-based Research at the Department of Public Health at Aarhus University with main sites at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Oxford and satellite sites at several research institutions. You can read more about SMARTbiomed here.

The Centre aims to support methodological research and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The broad methodological focus is used to answer questions relevant to common complex diseases/disorders specifically cardiometabolic, brain, and infertility and reproductive health. It leverages large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods, including machine learning and AI, to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease. SMARTbiomed supports a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis of, and inference from, human health-related massive data, advancing applications in medicine.

The main objectives of SMARTbiomed are to bring together multi-disciplinary teams to develop new methods and apply them in biomedical research motivated by problems in clinical practice, develop data platforms and software for biomedical data science, and to deliver world-leading training and career development in health data science.

Your profile
We are seeking a distinguished and visionary academic leader at Full Professor level with an internationally recognised research profile in an area central to SMARTbiomed. This is a unique opportunity to shape the Centre’s scientific direction, strategic development and long-term success. SMARTbiomed unites leading research environments across three universities, supported by major philanthropic foundations, providing an exceptional platform for interdisciplinary collaboration, scientific innovation and impact. You will bring:

• Strategic academic leadership: Substantial experience in academic leadership and research management, ideally in ambitious, collaborative research environments.
• Scientific excellence: An outstanding research track record and comprehensive knowledge of relevant methods, tools and international best practice within SMARTbiomed’s scientific areas.
• Visionary and collaborative leadership: The ability to inspire, communicate clearly and navigate complex challenges with a constructive, solution-oriented approach.
• Strategic resource management: Experience in developing effective structures, managing resources and enabling researchers and research environments to thrive.
• Funding and partnerships: A proven ability to attract significant competitive external funding and develop ambitious research initiatives and collaborations.

Your role
As a senior leader of SMARTbiomed, you will have a key role in shaping the Centre’s scientific and strategic direction and in realising its ambition to develop an internationally leading research environment. You will be a highly visible and motivating leader who fosters a culture characterised by trust, collaboration, intellectual ambition and academic excellence. You will be based at the Department of Public Health at Aarhus University while playing an active leadership role across SMARTbiomed’s different sites and partner institutions. A central part of your role will be to connect people, disciplines and research environments across the Centre and across Denmark, accelerating the translation of research into solutions that benefit society and healthcare.

You will champion a diverse, inclusive and intellectually stimulating research environment in which talented researchers and staff are encouraged to develop, collaborate and pursue ambitious scientific ideas. Through engaged and visionary leadership, you will contribute to making SMARTbiomed a highly attractive environment for recruiting, developing and retaining outstanding researchers and staff. You will report to the leader of the National Centre for Register-based Research.

Key responsibilities include:

• Shape the scientific vision and set the overall agenda for SMARTbiomed, in collaboration with the co-directors, and translate the vision into a clear programme.
• Strengthen relationships with key stakeholders, including the major foundations funding SMARTbiomed, the universities and institutions involved in the Centre, and other strategic partners.
• Foster a strong culture of collaboration, inclusion and shared purpose across SMARTbiomed, ensuring that colleagues feel connected regardless of location or site.
• Lead the overall development and strategic management of SMARTbiomed, while ensuring effective day-to-day management and fulfilment of the Centre’s commitments to its funders and partners.
• Drive the expansion of SMARTbiomed’s research portfolio and funding base, while supporting researchers in developing ambitious research agendas and securing external funding.
• Build the visibility of SMARTbiomed, through active engagement with the academic community and funders, and unite the Danish research community, creating a foundation for societal impact and translation.
An attractive start package can be negotiated.

About the Department of Public Health
The Department of Public Health is a research-intensive environment dedicated to advancing scientific knowledge and developing applied solutions to major public health challenges. Research at the department spans theoretical, basic, and applied sciences, with the shared ambition of generating impactful knowledge and improving population health. Academic excellence is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to conducting rigorous and innovative research and delivering high-quality teaching. Rooted in our respective disciplines, we foster interdisciplinary collaboration to strengthen research, education and innovation. We are equally committed to cultivating a healthy and supportive workplace characterised by open dialogue, mutual respect and an informal atmosphere. We believe that academic excellence and personal well-being are mutually reinforcing and essential to long-term success. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Questions about the position

Terms of employment

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Experimental Clearance Flow Research - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
The PhD candidate will, as part of a collaboration project between a private enterprise and DTU Construct, carry out experimental clearance flow research with ammonia and other sustainable marine fuels. 

Pressure and temperature conditions, resembling those in a marine engine booster pump, are created in an in-house designed clearance flow test rig. Measured clearance flow data will be used to develop and validate accurate flow models. The test rig will be further modified to enable testing and evaluation of different sealing solutions.

Responsibilities and qualifications

The PhD candidate will be responsible for continuing our development of a high-pressure ammonia flow rig, conduct test campaigns with different ammonia pump components and develop both theoretical and experimental foundation for developing ammonia compatible sealing techniques.

The candidate should have significant experience with:

• Safe handling of ammonia and other liquified gases in test setups.
• Design and wiring electronic data acquisition and control systems using PC Schematics.
• LabView programming.
• Mechanical design and FEM analysis using Solid Works.
• Data processing of large experimental sets of dynamic flow and pressure data using statistical methods in Matlab.
• CMM (Coordinate Measurement Machine) measurement and preferably have experience with Calypso Software.
• Data processing large complex geometric data sets from CMM measurements for 3-dimensional analysis of tested pump components.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

 (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)

  Department of Clinical Medicine
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint a clinical professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology to commence as soon as possible. The externally funded professorship is combined with a consultancy at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet, Department of ORL, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology in the Capital Region.

  Both the professorship and the consultancy will be financed by Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

• Academic assessments   Required qualifications

• Manage research and other management functions, e.g. engage in the university’s external academic activities, as well as knowledge and technology transfer

  For the professorship the appointee will receive a pensionable annual honorarium of 219.882,33 DKK (1 August 2026 level).

  Questions
 For further information please contact Head of Department Nicolai W. Albrechtsen, nicolai.albrechtsen@regionh.dk.

• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD and other relevant certificates)
